questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(2,1,3)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $3x-6y-6z=-15.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=1$ and $y=-1$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-6y-6z & =-15 \\ 3(1)-6(-1)-6z & =-15 \\ -6z & =-24 \\ z & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(1,-1,4)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,-1,4⟩-⟨2,1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨3,-6,-6⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot (-6)+1\cdot (-6)|}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+(-6)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-3+12-6|}{\sqrt{9+36+36}} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{81}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(2,7,20)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨6,-9,3⟩=51.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨6,-9,3⟩ & =51 \\ 6x-9y+3z & =51 \\ 3z & =51-6x+9y \\ z & =17-2x+3y.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $x=1$ and $y=2,$ we get 

$$
z=17-2(1)+3(2)=21.
$$

So, the point $Q(1,2,21)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,2,21⟩-⟨2,7,20⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨6,-9,3⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot 6+(-5)\cdot (-9)+1\cdot 3|}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-9)^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-6+45+3|}{\sqrt{36+81+9}} \\  & =\frac{|42|}{\sqrt{126}} \\  & =\sqrt{14}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(6,6,2)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $4x-7y-4z=-26.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=1$ and $y=2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-7y-4z & =-26 \\ 4(1)-7(2)-4z & =-26 \\ -4z & =-16 \\ z & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(1,2,4)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,2,4⟩-⟨6,6,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-5,-4,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨4,-7,-4⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-5)\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot (-7)+2\cdot (-4)|}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-7)^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-20+28-8|}{\sqrt{16+49+16}} \\  & =\frac{|\,0\,|}{\sqrt{81}} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point $P$ lies on the plane.

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(5,3,7)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩=16.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a point on the plane. If $r=⟨x,y,z⟩,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,-3,6⟩ & =16 \\ -2x-3y+6z & =16 \\ 2x & =6z-3y-16 \\ x & =3z-\frac{3}{2}y-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting $y=2$ and $z=1,$ we get 

$$
x=3-\frac{3}{2}(2)-8=-8.
$$

So, the point $Q(-8,2,1)$ lies on the plane. 

Now, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-8,2,1⟩-⟨5,3,7⟩ \\  & =⟨-13,-1,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $n=⟨-2,-3,6⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-13)\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot (-3)+(-6)\cdot 6|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|26+3-36|}{\sqrt{4+9+36}} \\  & =\frac{|-7|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{7}{7} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,1,5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-2x+4y+4z=18.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-1$ and $y=2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x+4y+4z & =18 \\ -2(-1)+4(2)+4z & =18 \\ 4z & =8 \\ z & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,2,2)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-1,2,2⟩-⟨-2,1,5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-2,4,4⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 4+(-3)\cdot 4|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-2+4-12|}{\sqrt{4+16+16}} \\  & =\frac{|-10|}{\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{10}{6} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
